1.Complete records are not always maintained for periodic calibration of laboratory instruments, apparatus, gauges, and
recording devices.
For all High Performance Liquid Chromatography systems (HPLC), the firm failed to monitor the lamp hours of their UV
detectors. In addition, monitoring of the QC laboratory’s HPLC units does not include a periodic check of the hours of the UV-
Vis lamps after 2000 hours of operation as recommended by the manufacturer. For example, six (6) of the HPLC units, QC-
170, QC-169, QC-024, QC-026, QC-122 and QC-021, showed operational hours of 13,003 hours, 11,132 hours, 5,106 hours,
3,475 hours, 3,198 hours, and 2,371 hours respectively without the lamps being replaced or being reset to zero after changing of
the lamp.
2. Laboratory records do not include a complete record of all data secured in the course of each test, including all
hromatograms from laboratory instrumentation, properly identified to show the specific components of the drug substance
tested. Specifically, laboratory records do not always contain the HPLC standard and sample chromatograms. For example, the
laboratory records for
USP Batch #4
manufactured 2/25/2017, #2
manufactured
2/23/2017 &™
manufactured 2/22/2017, did not include the HPLC standard and sample chromatograms for Assay
and Related Substances instead only results summary reports are attached. The chromatographic data was limited to calculated
results for last
3 months.
